title: DevExp integration lag: root cause and follow-ups
content:
TL;DR: On 2026-04-27 we saw a sustained spike in developer-reported integration latencies for the JS and Go quickstart flows (median p95 latency from samples environment jumped from ~230ms to ~1.6s). After triage we found two compounding causes: an HTTP proxy misconfiguration introduced retry storms for 502s, and our quickstarts/sample apps were pinning the old SDK transport behavior (no connection pooling + no correlation headers), which magnified tail latency and made debugging hard. This doc is a lightweight postmortem + action list from the DevExp standup on 2026-04-28.

Symptoms observed
- 2026-04-27 09:10 UTC: first customer Slack thread reporting "sdk quickstart extremely slow" from internal integrator account
- 2026-04-27 09:20 UTC: automated smoke tests for samples repo (samples-ci) began failing intermittently with 502/504
- P50 remained okay; p95 and p99 across quickstart flows rose to ~1.4–2.0s
- Error pattern: upstream 502 followed by rapid client retry attempts (exponential backoff not configured in some sample apps)
- Correlation: only hosted-region X showed the pattern; other regions normal

Initial hypotheses considered (from triage)
- infra regression in serving runtime change (unlikely: infra deploys at 02:00 UTC and was stable)
- model/encoder bug causing spike (no model changes on that date)
- network/proxy regression or config drift in region X (confirmed by SRE)
- sample code anti-patterns causing repeated retries and extra latency (confirmed by devexp review)

Root cause analysis (what we nailed down)
1) Network/proxy misconfiguration in region X
   - A new edge proxy deployment (PR: infra/edge#549) accidentally toggled the upstream connection timeout to a lower value (3s -> 1s) for a subset of routes. This caused transient 502s when the router retried upstream or when the runtime experienced a short GC pause.
   - Proxy also had aggressive retry policy enabled for idempotent routes; with SDKs and sample apps issuing concurrent requests, the retries amplified load (retry storm) and created a feedback loop.
2) Sample/quickstart anti-patterns
   - The JS quickstart (samples/quickstarts/js) instantiated a fresh HTTP client per request (no keepalive/agent pooling), so each retry incurred connection setup cost.
   - The Go quickstart explicitly re-tried on any 5xx without jitter or max attempts (in sample code comments: "simplified for readability")
   - Neither sample injected X-Request-Id or trace headers by default, making cross-service correlation during triage painful.
3) Telemetry blind spots
   - Our sampling of quickstart telemetry did not capture correlation IDs (sdk telemetry opt-in was disabled in sample templates).
   - Logs in the proxy lacked the downstream correlation id because SDKs did not send it.

Timeline (brief)
- 2026-04-27 09:25 UTC: Eng-Exp receives initial Slack alert
- 09:40 UTC: On-call SRE identifies a config drift in edge proxy; roll-back scheduled
- 10:05 UTC: Samples CI failing; devexp starts reproducing locally
- 11:10 UTC: Confirmed combination of proxy and sample retry behavior
- 13:00 UTC: Emergency proxy rollback (partial) -> region X p95 reduced to ~600ms
- 16:20 UTC: Full rollback completed; p95 approaching baseline
- 2026-04-28 devexp standup: agreed on action items and runbook draft

Impact
- Internal integrator customers experienced degraded UX for ~4–6 hours depending on region
- Several internal quickstart demos failed during hackday sessions
- No data loss or user data exposure

Resolutions applied
- Fast rollback of proxy config in region X to previous safe timeout
- Hotfix PR merged to samples repo: add connection pooling to JS agent and add bounded retry with jitter in Go sample
- Temporary documentation note added to quickstart readme warning about naive retry loops

Action items (owners and targets)
- A1: Add correlation headers by default in SDK quickstarts (X-Request-Id + traceparent). Owner: Samir Patel. Due: 2026-05-03. Notes: align with tracing spec, include example of propagating header from front-end.
- A2: Update sample templates to use persistent HTTP agent / keepalive for JS + default client reuse for Python and Go. Owner: Ethan Brooks. Due: 2026-05-06.
- A3: Add sample CI test that simulates proxy 502s and ensures samples back off with jitter. Owner: Marina Duarte. Due: 2026-05-12.
- A4: Instrument SDK to emit a correlation id in telemetry when present and make it easy to enable in samples (feature flag). Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-05-10.
- A5: DevExp runbook: "handling proxy-induced retry storms" — include checklist and rollback play. Owner: Olivia Chen (SRE liaison). Due: 2026-05-05.
- A6: Docs quick win: Update quickstarts to call out "Do not blindly retry on 5xx" with code snippets. Owner: Docs team (cc: devexp). Due: 2026-05-04.

Short-term mitigations (already done)
- Proxy rollback in region X
- PRs merged to samples repo with cautious retry/backoff and keepalive
- Slack #devexp pinned note with reproducer steps and the incident timeline

Longer-term proposals (discussed in standup)
- Default trace propagation in all SDKs, plus a small quickstart page showing end-to-end trace correlation (console -> SDK -> proxy -> runtime) with screenshots
- Add a synthetic monitoring job in Optimize that exercises quickstart flows every hour and validates latency and response shapes
- Add a linter in samples repo that flags anti-patterns: fresh-client-per-request, infinite retries, missing correlation headers
- Consider SDK changes to expose safer retry primitives (e.g., RetryPolicy object with jittered backoff) rather than examples in samples only

Open questions / unresolved
- Do we want correlation headers by default in hosted API responses? (privacy / telemetry implications)
- Should the SDK default to a safe RetryPolicy or keep the current opt-in behavior? (backwards compatibility)
- How to balance readability of quickstart examples vs demonstrating production-safe patterns? Proposed: keep two examples per language: "concise for learning" + "production-ready snippet".

Notes-to-self / meeting flavor
- Keep the standup short; this doc is the canonical follow-up for the cross-team owners
- Make sure SRE signs off on runbook before we mark anything as "final"
- Olivia: please loop in infra-security if we touch header defaults (privacy)

Quick checklist for next standup
- [ ] Samir: PR to add trace header in SDK samples (link + status)
- [ ] Ethan: samples keepalive PR merged to main
- [ ] Marina: CI test implemented in samples-ci
- [ ] Priya: telemetry patch and feature flag deployed to samples staging
- [ ] Olivia: runbook draft in Confluence and review scheduled

Relevant links (copied during triage)
- reproducer script: github.com/redwood-inference/samples/quickstart-repro (branch: proxy-replay)
- infra PR that caused config drift: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/549
- samples hotfix PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/319 and /320

If anything else shows up in the next 48h we escalate to SEV-2 and follow the runbook.

-- end of notes (DevExp standup 2026-04-28)
